This is due to two reasons:

- Shadows are disabled on DirectionalLight3D, so dynamic objects don't receive real-time shadows.
  - If you want to avoid the cost of dynamic lighting entirely, you would need https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8040 to be implemented so that both direct and indirect light is baked into probes. This way, the light can be turned off entirely for real-time rendering.
- Dynamic indirect light is interpolating with probes located at the edges of the geometry, which are outdoors and receive outdoor lighting:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4eb8da4-a300-47a1-9289-2f95711f9b31)

If you add more probes in the corners, remove the one in the center and enable shadows on DirectionalLight3D, it'll look much closer already:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec603b77-1097-4677-a996-c02b44aad5f1)

It still looks brighter here because reflections are sampled from the outside sky, even though the object is indoor. This can be addressed by adding a ReflectionProbe indoors or using https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86102.

It's technically possible to have automatically placed probes moved towards scene geometry corners (as mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7938), but it's nontrivial to implement.

MRP with the changes: [lightmap-colors-2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18825873/lightmap-colors-2.zip)
why does subdiv off still generate 8 corner probes? its in the code for lightmap gi with no explanation. feels like this might be the real problem

> why does subdiv off still generate 8 corner probes? its in the code for lightmap gi with no explanation. feels like this might be the real problem

Corner probes are always generated because the shader that renders lightmaps expects probe data to be available within its bounds. If no probes were placed at the corners, then probes placed in the center would have nothing to interpolate to.

However, checking **Interior** on LightmapGI appears to have no effect on generated probes (nor environment lighting on that matter, despite its description):

Interior *Off* | Interior *On*
-|-
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffba2b80-3e25-448f-af0f-7820722f975d) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92525baf-5ff6-44c7-a430-9688c011e125)

This is what setting `interior` in LightmapGI does:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e948f52ea93cfff23b4a24b83d310724be2fb208/scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp#L231

`interior` is not used anywhere in `*.glsl` files, and it isn't used in `lightmapper_rd.cpp` either. It is however used here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e948f52ea93cfff23b4a24b83d310724be2fb208/servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp#L2136

(Note that it's not used in Compatibility, only in Forward+/Mobile.)

In comparison, this is with **Environment > Mode** set to **Disabled** on the LightmapGI node:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50e91765-89b3-422e-ac33-6c731e3b18d3)

When environment lighting isn't baked, dynamic object lighting closely matches static objects, even with a single central probe:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d6663d5-62f1-4f52-b146-601c6525ad0f)

I guess checking **Interior** should make it so that probes placed at the corners are fully black to avoid this kind of interpolation issue.

> interior is not used anywhere in *.glsl files, and it isn't used in lightmapper_rd.cpp either.

Not sure what this would be expected to do even, light behaves the same indoors as it does outdoors. To me it feels like that property might as well just be deprecated since it seems to serve no purpose. I don't like having behavior tied to indoor vs outdoor properties since this makes mixed scenes super painful to create, so I'm not in favor of adding new functionality that relies on that checkbox. Ideally we strive for no "interior" checkbox, and have things work as nicely as possible out of the box without that distinction. This is a good example of a solution for the same issue (reliance on interior vs exterior) on reflection probes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3013#issuecomment-2501082143


> I guess checking Interior should make it so that probes placed at the corners are fully black to avoid this kind of interpolation issue.

This seems like a workaround that works for this particular MRP, but wouldn't fix the same issue in most scenes. Pretty much anytime the corners of the indoor scene don't line up exactly with the corners of the probes would still give you the same issue.

As you said before, I think this is more of an problem rooted in the current probe spawning behavior, and I think improvements to manual and/or automatic probe placement, maybe combined with some documentation guidance on how to deal with this situation, would be more fruitful/productive solutions to tackle this issue. :)

Relevant PRs:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103781
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/83420
